problem_statement: Robpayot/webgl-distortion-bulge-effect is a Vite + OGL WebGL demo (a Codrops bulge-distortion tutorial) with two routes: Demo 1 (index.html, '/') scrolls a column of image cards and Demo 2 (index2.html, '/index2.html') hovers circular cards, each backed by an OGL Triangle shader with uRadius / uStrength / uBulge uniforms driven by mousemove and lil-gui. A shared 'Card texture browser' control panel is mounted in normal flow at the top of <main> on both routes (the OGL card and background canvases are fixed/absolute, so the panel is the only normal-flow chrome). The panel has a filter tab row (All / Portraits / Landscapes / Abstract), a live read-out line, and a grid of eight texture chips (image-1.jpg .. image-8.jpg); clicking a filter tab dims the non-matching texture chips and updates the read-out to 'Showing N of 8 . <Category>'. Three faults were reported and must all be repaired in the shared panel sources: (1) on a 390px mobile viewport the panel's fixed-width no-wrap tab row and chip grid overrun the screen and force horizontal page scrolling; (2) the panel is only mounted on Demo 1 and is missing from Demo 2; (3) clicking a filter tab leaves the read-out frozen at 'Showing 8 of 8 . All textures' and never dims the non-matching chips. Restore the panel so it fits every viewport, appears on both demo routes, and the filter recomputes the read-out and chip filtering on every click, while keeping both WebGL demos exactly as-is.
required_content: Fix src/shared/hud.scss so the Card texture browser filter tab row and texture chip grid do not cause horizontal overflow at 390px mobile width on either demo route (content right-edge within the viewport, tolerance 24px), by letting the rows wrap / flex rather than clipping a still-too-wide fixed row.

Fix src/shared/hud.scss so the panel reads as a clean control on desktop and tablet: the filter tabs and the eight texture chips lay out in a legible, non-overlapping grid (no shingled/negative-margin pile, no dark-on-dark or white-on-white text).
Fix src/shared/hudSurfaces.js so the Card texture browser is mounted on BOTH Demo 1 and Demo 2 (the shared control must appear on every route, not only Demo 1).

Fix src/shared/hud.js so clicking a filter tab recomputes the read-out to 'Showing N of 8 . <Category>' for the clicked category and dims the non-matching texture chips (the read-out must not stay frozen at the initial 'Showing 8 of 8 . All textures').

Keep both WebGL demos intact: the frame header/nav, the OGL card and background canvases, the hover bulge interaction, and the Demo 1 / Demo 2 navigation, plus all eight texture chip names (image-1.jpg .. image-8.jpg) and the four filter tabs (All / Portraits / Landscapes / Abstract).
design_constraints: The panel markup (the .hud section in index.html / index2.html) is shared and unchanged; the repair lives in the three shared panel sources: src/shared/hud.scss (layout + responsive + contrast), src/shared/hud.js (filter wiring + read-out), src/shared/hudSurfaces.js (which demo routes mount the panel).
Do not merely clip overflow (overflow-x:hidden on a still-too-wide no-wrap row leaves the layout overflowing); let the tab row and chip grid wrap or flex so the real content fits a 390px phone.

The filter tabs and eight texture chips must render as a legible, non-overlapping grid on desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px): rounded tab pills and rounded chip cards, consistent gap spacing, a dark active-tab fill with white label text, dark chip titles on a light chip background, and the green read-out line — no shingled negative-margin overlap and no dark-on-dark or white-on-white text.
Do not break the Vite build, the OGL/GSAP/lil-gui shader pipeline, or the two demo routes.
Desktop (1440px), tablet (834px) and 390px mobile states on both demos must have no horizontal overflow.
state_constraints: desktop_demo1_initial loads Demo 1 at 1440px: the Card texture browser renders its filter tabs and eight texture chips as a legible, non-overlapping grid with no horizontal overflow.
tablet_demo1_initial checks Demo 1 at 834px with no horizontal overflow.
mobile_demo1_initial checks Demo 1 at 390px and MUST have no horizontal overflow (repaired behaviour; the buggy baseline overflows here).
desktop_demo1_filter clicks the 'Landscapes' filter tab on Demo 1: the read-out becomes 'Showing 3 of 8 . Landscapes' and the non-Landscapes chips dim (the frozen-read-out control fails this).
desktop_demo2_initial loads Demo 2 at 1440px: the Card texture browser is present here too (cross-route), with no horizontal overflow.
tablet_demo2_initial checks Demo 2 at 834px with no horizontal overflow.
mobile_demo2_initial checks Demo 2 at 390px and MUST have no horizontal overflow (repaired behaviour; the buggy baseline overflows here too).
desktop_demo2_hover hovers the first circular card on Demo 2 so the OGL bulge interaction runs; the panel content is unchanged.

change_completion: The Card texture browser no longer causes horizontal overflow at 390px mobile on either demo.
Clicking a filter tab updates the read-out to 'Showing N of 8 . <Category>' and dims non-matching texture chips.
design_consistency: The filter tabs and eight texture chips lay out as a legible, non-overlapping grid on desktop and tablet.
Text contrast is readable (no dark-on-dark or white-on-white); no shingled negative-margin chip pile.
regression: No existing behaviour regresses: both WebGL demos keep their frame header/nav, OGL card and background canvases, the hover bulge interaction, the eight texture chip names, and the Demo 1 / Demo 2 navigation, all preserved unchanged.
The Vite build, the two demo routes, and the OGL/GSAP/lil-gui shader pipeline remain intact and are not broken or regressed by the repair.
responsive: Both demos have no horizontal overflow on desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile.
The filter tab row and texture chip grid reflow and stay readable at 390px mobile.
evaluation_rubric.scoring_notes: A correct patch fixes the three shared panel sources so the Card texture browser (a) fits a 390px phone by wrapping its filter tab row and texture chip grid, (b) is mounted on BOTH Demo 1 and Demo 2, and (c) recomputes the read-out ('Showing N of 8 . <Category>') and dims non-matching chips on every filter click, while keeping both WebGL demos intact. The buggy baseline keeps the fixed-width 720px no-wrap rows (overflows mobile) and mounts the panel on Demo 1 only (missing on Demo 2), but its filter wiring is correct. The known-bad control additionally collapses the panel into an illegible overlapping pile (shingled chips, dark-on-dark / white-on-white) and freezes the read-out at 'Showing 8 of 8 . All textures' on click, so it fails no_horizontal_overflow, visual_regression, dom_assertions (missing on Demo 2), and interaction_assertions.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Robpayot/webgl-distortion-bulge-effect is a runnable Vite + OGL WebGL demo with two shader routes. Its shared Card texture browser control panel is the demo's own native affordance for choosing which of the eight card textures the bulge shader highlights (a filter tab row + live read-out + eight texture chips), placed in normal flow because the OGL canvases are fixed/absolute. That makes it an ideal regression_continuity Repair task independent of the WebGL canvas: the reference wraps the rows (0 mobile overflow), mounts the panel on both routes, and recomputes the filter read-out; the buggy baseline keeps fixed no-wrap rows and drops the panel from Demo 2; and a known-bad control collapses the grid into an illegible overlapping pile and freezes the read-out on click.

author_notes: Repo-grounded repair / regression_continuity / cross_page task on the Vite + OGL WebGL bulge-distortion demo by Robin Payot. The native lever is the demo's own Card texture browser control panel: a filter tab row (All / Portraits / Landscapes / Abstract), a live read-out, and a grid of eight texture chips (image-1.jpg .. image-8.jpg) that map to the OGL card meshes. The reference wraps the tab row and chip grid (flex-wrap:wrap, flex 1 1 150px, min-width:0) so there is zero horizontal overflow at 390px on either demo, mounts the browser on both routes, and recomputes the read-out and chip dimming on every filter click. The baseline is the buggy original: fixed-width 720px no-wrap tab row and chip grid (overflows mobile) and a route whitelist that mounts the panel on Demo 1 only (missing from Demo 2), but its filter JS is correct so its read-out still updates. The known-bad control collapses the whole panel into a broken overlapping pile (shingled chips with negative margins, near-white tabs on near-white, near-black text on a near-black panel) and freezes the read-out at 'Showing 8 of 8 . All textures' on click, so it fails no_horizontal_overflow, visual_regression, cross-route dom_assertions and interaction_assertions. Three shared sources vary across legs: src/shared/hud.scss, src/shared/hud.js, src/shared/hudSurfaces.js. The demo2 .text__words ambient overflow and the html overflow-x clip are neutralized as build infrastructure identical across all three legs, so the reference runtime is console/network clean (only benign swiftshader WebGL GL-driver warnings, not counted).
